newsitem.title: ERITREA: Eritrea denies it involved in attacks on Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Eritrea denies it involved in attacks on Sudan.

text.p: Eritrea on Thursday rejected accusations by Sudan that its troops had joined rebels in attacks on eastern Sudanese border posts.
Sudanese rebels meanwhile said they were continuing an assault on government positions with great success.
Eritrean Foreign Minister Petros Solomon also described as an "absolute lie" a Sudanese claim that Khartoum forces killed Eritrean soldiers in fighting along its eastern frontiers.

Sudan on Wednesday accused Eritrea and government rebels of attacks on Sudanese border posts, saying that it lost seven of its own soldiers and killed 200 Eritrean troops in separate battles near their border.
"It's an absolute lie. There were no Eritreans involved," Petros told Reuters in the Eritrean capital of Asmara.

Yassir Arman, spokesman of the rebel Sudan Peoples' Liberation Army in Asmara, also accused the Sudanese government of lying. "This is mere propaganda. Firstly, there is no Eritrean involvement," Arman told Reuters.
Eritrea hosts groups opposed to the Sudanese government.

Arman repeated a rebel claim to have captured a Sudanese military garrison at Gadamyeeb, northeast of Kassala town which is close to the Eritrean border and lies about 280 miles (450 km) east of the Sudanese capital.
"Our forces are now attacking Gotned and advancing since yesterday toward Tukan," he added.
Tukan is a small community near Kassala. Gotned is also in Kassala state.

Sudan's Islamist military government has called for mobilisation against what it says are Ethiopian and rebel assaults on eastern Sudan, but it was the first time in this round of conflict that it also accused neighbouring Eritrea.
There have been no independent reports from the area.
The Sudanese army confirmed that its forces had been shelled in Gotned on January 14.

Sudanese government spokesman Brigadier al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair, in a separate statement, said a battalion had been attacked in the Hamaskhoureb area, southeast of Kassala. Khair said they killed "over 200 enemy troops".
